    Semaglutide vs tirzepatide: what online clinics charge for each.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 8 Nov 2026.

    Short answer

    Semaglutide from $49/mo at 37 clinics1 and tirzepatide from $90/mo at 26 clinics2, checked 8 Nov 2026. Brand plans start at Wegovy from $1493 and Zepbound from $3494. Wegovy and Zepbound are FDA approved for weight management; Ozempic and Mounjaro are approved for type 2 diabetes.5678 Compounded copies are not FDA approved.9

    What are semaglutide and tirzepatide?

    Both act on the body's receptors for gut hormones. Semaglutide acts on one, the GLP-1 receptor;7 tirzepatide acts on two, the GIP and GLP-1 receptors.8

    Each is sold under more than one brand name: semaglutide as Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy, tirzepatide as Mounjaro and Zepbound.1011

    Which brands are approved for weight loss?

    • Wegovy (semaglutide): to reduce excess body weight and keep it off in adults with obesity, or with overweight and a weight-related condition, and to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke in some adults.5
    • Zepbound (tirzepatide): to reduce excess body weight and keep it off in the same groups, and to treat moderate to severe sleep apnea in adults with obesity.6
    • Ozempic (semaglutide): for blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes, and to lower heart risk in some of them.7
    • Mounjaro (tirzepatide): for blood sugar in adults and children aged 10 and over with type 2 diabetes.8

    Some clinics sell Ozempic plans too, as the table below shows. The label tells you what the FDA approved each brand for.

    What does the care fee add?

    Under each price is the clinic's care fee: "all-in" when the price includes the prescriber and check-ins, "incl." and a monthly amount when the clinic charges one on top, already added into the price, or "care fee not known" when the clinic's page did not say. 10 of the plans above add a fee on top.

    What does the price not tell you?

    • Whether the price goes up as the dose goes up. Ask the clinic.
    • For a compounded plan, which pharmacy makes it. The FDA does not check a compounded medicine before it is sold.9
    • Whether a compounded semaglutide is a salt form, which the FDA says is a different ingredient from the one in the approved drugs.98

    Our guides on compounded semaglutide prices and compounded vs brand GLP-1 go further. None of this is medical advice; your prescriber can tell you which medicine fits you.
